- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -1.0) and prices are falling, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply a 1–2% upward bias for first 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 2–5% to align with historical volatility.
- For sentiment-neutral periods, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment shifts.
